text:
Global transition graphs aggregate item-pair evidence across users; GCL4SR provides a concrete example of weighted transitions and degree normalization ([paper](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2022/0333.pdf)). The clearest evidence about target-edge memorization comes from adjacent link-prediction research: SpotTarget distinguishes training-target inclusion, which encourages overfitting and train–inference distribution shift, from held-out-target inclusion, which leaks evaluation information ([study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00899)). Thus, using exclusively permitted training histories is legitimate fitting, but measuring training-target recovery on that same graph can be optimistic. A validation transition independently supported by other training users is legitimate evidence; incorporating the held-out interaction itself is leakage.

I found no direct evidence that leave-one-user-out or user-fold cross-fitting is an established diagnostic standard for sequential transition graphs. As a methodological adaptation, compare each training target’s score/rank under the full graph with its result under a graph excluding that user’s contributions. User-level exclusion removes repeated evidence from the same history while preserving corroboration from others. Alternatively, partition training users into folds, construct each diagnostic graph from the other folds, and score excluded users. Report paired changes in HR@10, target rank, and transition support, especially for singleton and low-support transitions. These quantify dependence on self-contributed graph evidence, not validation leakage.

For additive transition counts, inexpensive diagnostics subtract sparse per-user or per-fold counts from cached global counts, then recompute affected normalization and pruning. Sample users or targets instead of exhaustively rebuilding graphs. Removing only one transition occurrence is cheaper but misses repeated self-evidence. With learned graph encoders, frozen-weight graph ablations measure structural sensitivity; they do not remove memorization already stored in parameters. Full cross-fitted retraining offers stronger isolation at substantially greater cost.
